heard: A tiny dwarf galaxy is wildly igniting massive new stars. Most astronomers thought small galaxies grew calm as they aged. Astronomer William Herschel spotted Caldwell 21 in 1788, millions of light-years away. This irregular galaxy belongs to a cluster in Keynes' Banatici. Gravitational poles from nearby neighbors violently squeezed its gas. Glowing pink clouds now mark active nurseries flaring across its core. That intense cosmic collision forced this tiny galaxy to wildly ignite stars.
differences: 'canes venatici' heard as 'keynes banatici' after 'a cluster in'
